full_judgment:
Md. Ashfaqul Islam, J: At the instance of the preemptee-petitioner this rule was issued calling upon the preemptor-opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 07.10.2002 passed by the District Judge, Brahmanbaria in Miscellaneous Appeal No.26 of 2002 allowing the appeal after setting aside the order dated 17.2.2002 passed by the Assistant Judge, Nabinagar in Miscellaneous Case No.28 of 2000 (under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure) rejecting the said case and also setting aside the order dated 14.5.2000 passed in Preemption Miscellaneous Case No.45 of 1994 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and restored the said case to its file and number should not be set aside and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may deem fit and proper. 

 2. The short facts for purpose of disposal of the rule is that the present opposite party along with 4 others as preemptor filed an application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act being Miscellaneous Case No.45 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Nabinagar, Brahmanbaria against the present petitioner and others. 

 4. The said miscellaneous case filed by the preemptor-petitioner under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure was contested by the preemptee-petitioner by filing written objection denying all the material statements made in the said application. This application was filed on 13.6.2000. 

 11. The decision spelt out by the apex Court is that no appeal lies against an order dismissing an application made under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoring a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which is dismissed for default. The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act does not provide for any appeal for such an order i.e. the order passed in an application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure dismissing the same for default which springs out of a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The reason is well founded because Order 43(1)(c ) contemplates that an appeal shall lie against an order under Order 9 rule 9 rejecting an application which must spring out from a suit but the proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act cannot be termed as suit and as such the appeal cannot be preferred against such order. Moreover, section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure in its strict term cannot be said to have been made applicable in this regard.
